The Olu of Oko Baba Agba in the Oworonshoki community of Lagos State, Oba Kabiru Adesegun Basiru, has appealed a court ruling nullifying his appointment and installation, as he seeks to proceed with his planned coronation on November 16. The monarch also filed an application for a stay of execution, an injunction pending appeal and other preservatory orders following the November 6 decision of the Lagos State High Court. PUNCH Online reports that the court had granted an application for a mandatory injunction by the claimants in Suit No. ID/9885GCMW/2023, between Prince Adeniyi Saliu and six others and the Governor of Lagos State and four others. The ruling set aside Basiru’s nomination, appointment, approval and installation as the Olu of Oko Baba Agba and restrained him from parading or holding himself out as the monarch. However, in a Notice of Appeal dated November 6 and sighted by our correspondent on Monday, Basiru, through his counsel, D.A. Awosika, SAN & Partners, challenged the decision, citing what the lawyers described as substantial questions of law. In a statement issued on Monday by Oladimeji Olabode of Awosika SAN & Partners Chambers, the lawyers said the appeal and accompanying applications were intended to protect the interests of the community and its traditional institution. The lawyers urged residents and other stakeholders to respect the rule of law and avoid actions capable of disrupting peace in the community while the matter remained before the courts. “Consequently, we call on all concerned to respect the rule of law, exercise restraint and refrain from any action capable of disrupting the peace of the community or interfering with the orderly resolution of the issues before the courts,” the statement read. Acknowledging that the court’s decision might have generated concerns among residents and other stakeholders, the lawyers said there was no reason for panic or hostility. “We appreciate that recent developments may have generated questions and concerns among residents and other stakeholders. Nevertheless, there is no cause for panic, hostility or unnecessary apprehension,” they said. The lawyers also cautioned against intimidation, harassment, provocation, coercion and self-help, urging residents to continue their lawful daily activities without fear. “Oko Baba Agba is a community whose future should be founded on peace, mutual respect, unity and orderly administration. Whatever differences may exist, they should never become a source of hostility among neighbours or an obstacle to the progress and development of our community,” they said. They also urged residents to disregard sensational publications, avoid circulating unverified information and rely on credible updates as the legal proceedings continued. On the background to the dispute, the lawyers maintained that the establishment of the Oko Baba Agba chieftaincy stool followed recommendations by the Standing Tribunal of Inquiry into Chieftaincy Matters in Lagos State, chaired by Justice T. Ojikutiu-Oshode. According to the statement, the tribunal recommended the recognition of Oko Baba Agba as a distinct traditional community and the elevation of the Kekeniju Opemoluwa chieftaincy title in Oworonshoki to a second-class Obaship stool. It added that the Lagos State Executive Council subsequently approved and confirmed Basiru as the Olu of Oko Baba Agba, forming the basis for his appointment and installation. The lawyers said the monarch was dissatisfied with the court’s ruling and had taken the necessary legal steps to challenge it. “Our commitment remains to see the process through to its lawful conclusion and to the eventual realisation of the coronation of our Olu in accordance with the law,” the statement added.
